title: GitHub: cache and prioritize owned clone results
body:
Related to #141754.

This is a broader alternative to #310787. That PR fixes the immediate merge
ordering problem; this draft also explores making repository suggestions local-first
and persistent so repeated searches do not wait for GitHub again.

## Summary

- Add an optional Git Base remote-source change event so providers can return
  locally available results immediately and publish asynchronous updates later.
- Cache repository full names personally owned by the authenticated GitHub user in
  extension global storage. The cache is account-specific, written atomically, and
  contains no descriptions, star counts, or tokens.
- Rank personal repositories by exact name, prefix, then substring before matching
  public-search results.
- Debounce and cancel obsolete GitHub searches, cache completed searches briefly,
  and locally re-filter their results as the query changes.
- Validate the owned-repository cache hourly with an ETag and perform a full refresh
  daily. Clear account-specific state on account changes or sign-out.

## Motivation

The current clone picker waits for remote results and can rank a popular public
repository above a much more relevant personal repository. Repeating or narrowing a
query can also repeat the wait or temporarily remove still-valid suggestions.

This approach downloads the authenticated user's personally owned repository names
once, keeps them on disk, and filters/ranks them synchronously on every keystroke.
Public search remains available as a progressively loaded fallback.

## Scope question

This draft intentionally gives personally owned repositories priority over
organization and unrelated public repositories. It does not yet maintain an
organization-membership cache, so organization repositories discovered through
public search are ranked by match quality rather than membership. Before marking
this ready, I would like maintainer guidance on whether organization membership
should also be cached or exposed as a separate picker path, as discussed in
#141754.

## Testing

- GitHub remote-source provider tests: 16 passing.
- Git Base extension integration tests: 14 passing.
- TypeScript compilation for both changed extensions.
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript implementation/test files.
- Manual testing in an Extension Development Host with my GitHub account:
  - exact, prefix, and substring searches;
  - switching repeatedly between cached queries;
  - narrowing `transaction` to `transactio` without losing compatible results;
  - personal repositories ranking above organization/public results;
  - restart followed by an immediate result from the disk cache.

The full monorepo test suite has not been run.

## AI assistance disclosure

Most of this implementation was produced by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol with high reasoning
effort in Codex, under my supervision. I directed the behavior and performed several
functional and UX testing passes with my own GitHub account, but I have not yet done
a thorough line-by-line human code review. The PR is therefore intentionally a draft
while the approach and implementation receive closer review.

title: agentHost: route MCP auth during session initialization
body:
Fixes #329223

## Root cause

The Copilot runtime intentionally keeps host-injected MCP bearer tokens session-scoped: the embedding host owns refresh, revocation, persistence, and per-server consent. Agent Host therefore has to deliver the workbench's persisted grant to every SDK session that challenges.

Two races could lose that delivery:

1. A `CopilotAgentSession` can issue `onMcpAuthRequest` while `initializeSession()` is still running. The session was added to `_chatEntriesBySdkId` only after initialization completed, while `handleAuthenticationToken()` searched only that live map.
2. Workbench silent MCP authentication coalesced by server identity across sessions. A session challenging after the shared operation's host-side fan-out had been snapshotted reused the promise but did not perform its own delivery.

## Before/after evidence

### Before — shipped Insiders, pre-fix

A real new Agent Host chat on the affected build immediately challenged again for an MCP whose VS Code authentication session and access grant already existed:

```text
[Copilot:<new-session>] MCP server 'vscode-slack' requires authentication for https://mcp.slack.com
[AgentHost] MCP authentication succeeded for vscode-slack
```

The same startup trace contained repeated `requires authentication` → renderer token-delivery pairs for other previously authorized MCPs. This shows that persistence was intact in the workbench, but the token still had to be recovered again for each new SDK session—and could be lost in the initialization/coalescing races above.

### After — this branch

#### Real signed-in Slack OAuth E2E

I loaded an isolated plugin containing only the `github-slack` MCP definition, authorized it once through the real Slack browser OAuth flow, and then started two brand-new Agent Host sessions. Isolating the definition prevents a second Slack client registration from changing the provider identity during the test.

Before the one-time authorization, VS Code correctly showed the server as requiring authentication. After authorization, both later sessions completed without an auth card, browser redirect, or other user interaction, and the server remained running:

| Before one-time authorization | After authorization and two new sessions |
|---|---|
| ![github-slack requires authentication](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/076dc626-0f39-47e6-8c7f-c2e27a49f62b) | ![github-slack remains running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a38b032-2c02-40bb-b136-40837ee4f832) |

The two later sessions are visible here as separate completed chats:

![Two new sessions completed without another MCP authentication prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e19c300c-8267-4ca6-81ec-9c12b4909e85)

Each new SDK session still issued its expected session-scoped challenge. The workbench silently resolved that challenge from the persisted grant, and Slack reached `connected (ready)` in 326 ms and 350 ms respectively:

```text
Session 1
08:30:55.171 MCP server 'github-slack' requires authentication
08:30:55.176 [AgentHost] MCP authentication succeeded for github-slack
08:30:55.497 MCP server 'github-slack' connected (ready)

Session 2
08:32:34.101 MCP server 'github-slack' requires authentication
08:32:34.123 [AgentHost] MCP authentication succeeded for github-slack
08:32:34.451 MCP server 'github-slack' connected (ready)
```

The separate workspace-local `vscode-automation-mcp` error visible in the server list is unrelated to this test; the isolated test target is `github-slack`.

#### Deterministic lifecycle regression coverage

The regression tests start real `CopilotAgent` chat creation/resume paths with the fake SDK blocked inside `onMcpAuthRequest`, then deliver the persisted token through the real Agent Host authentication service:

- Two concurrently initializing new chats both receive `{ kind: 'token', accessToken: 'mcp-token' }` and both become live from one host-side fan-out.
- A later new chat performs its own persisted-token delivery instead of sharing an already-completed cross-session operation.
- Provisional materialization, default cold resume, and peer-chat resume all receive the token before registration completes.
- Insufficient scopes are rejected.
- Shutdown while blocked on authentication, and shutdown during post-initialization metadata work, both cancel without registering or leaking the session.
- Workbench coverage verifies two simultaneous sessions perform two target deliveries while the existing provider-level sequencer still serializes authentication-provider access.

Observed fixed-run result:

```text
CopilotAgent — MCP authentication during session initialization
  7 passing

AgentHostChatContribution — mcp auth prompt
  5 passing
```

That final lifecycle matrix passed **30/30 repeated executions**. No interactive Authenticate path is used in these successful cases.

## Change

- Track every Copilot session in a `DisposableSet` from SDK initialization until atomic ownership transfer to the live-session map.
- Centralize all four `initializeSession()` paths in one initialize/register helper so future paths cannot bypass tracking.
- Keep final client and working-directory validation synchronous with registration.
- Dispose initialization-blocked sessions during shutdown and reject registration when shutdown already removed ownership.
- Scope workbench silent-auth coalescing by URI comparison identity for the target session, so every session independently delivers its persisted grant while provider setup remains serialized by the existing authentication sequencer.
- Add production-path coverage for concurrent immediate creation, later repeated delivery, provisional materialization, default cold resume, peer resume, scope mismatch, authentication-blocked shutdown, and shutdown during post-initialization metadata work.

No protocol, SDK/runtime token-storage, token refresh, scope, consent, or revocation semantics are changed.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Targeted ESLint on all changed files
- `npm run hygiene` (full repository)
- `copilotAgent.test.ts`: 363 passing, 1 pending
- `CopilotAgentSession` MCP inventory: 27 passing
- Agent service authentication suite: 12 passing
- Agent Host MCP auth-prompt suite: 5 passing
- Agent Host service graph: 6 passing
- Final MCP lifecycle matrix: 30/30 repeated executions passed
- Copilot Agent Host E2E replay, run twice after the final lifecycle changes: 177 passing, 21 pending on each run

title: Local harness should honor `reasoning-effort` from custom `.agent.md` files
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Problem

Custom `.agent.md` files now support the `reasoning-effort` frontmatter property:

```yaml
---
name: Code-Review
model: GPT-5.6 Sol (copilot)
reasoning-effort: xhigh
---
```

However, the behavior currently differs depending on which harness executes the custom agent.

The Copilot Agent Host path forwards `reasoning-effort` to the Copilot SDK as `CustomAgentConfig.reasoningEffort`, as implemented in #329263.

The local VS Code chat harness does not appear to preserve or apply the same custom-agent reasoning-effort value.

In the local harness, `ICustomAgent` currently contains fields such as `model`, `tools`, and agent instructions, but not the configured reasoning effort. When `runSubagent` creates the child request, its `modelConfiguration` is resolved from the selected model configuration instead:

```ts
modelConfiguration: modeModelId
    ? this.languageModelsService.getModelConfiguration(modeModelId)
    : undefined,
```

As a result, the reasoning effort selected in the model picker / parent session is used even when the invoked custom agent explicitly declares a different `reasoning-effort`.

## Example

Given:

```yaml
# Code-Review.agent.md
---
name: Code-Review
model: GPT-5.6 Sol (copilot)
reasoning-effort: xhigh
---
```

and a parent session using:

```text
GPT-5.6 Sol
Reasoning effort: high
```

invoking `Code-Review` through the local `runSubagent` path currently results in the subagent running with:

```text
reasoning effort: high
```

rather than the expected:

```text
reasoning effort: xhigh
```

The same `.agent.md` property is honored by the Copilot Agent Host path.

## Expected behavior

`reasoning-effort` should have consistent semantics across custom-agent execution paths.

For both direct custom-agent execution and local `runSubagent` invocation:

1. If the custom agent declares a supported `reasoning-effort`, use that value.
2. If the custom agent does not declare one, inherit the current model/session configuration as today.
3. If a future explicit per-invocation reasoning-effort override is added to `runSubagent`, that explicit value should take precedence over the custom-agent default.

A reasonable precedence order would be:

```text
explicit per-invocation override
    >
custom .agent.md reasoning-effort
    >
picker / parent model configuration
    >
model default
```

## Suggested implementation

The local custom-agent representation could retain the parsed reasoning-effort value, for example:

```ts
export interface ICustomAgent {
    // ...
    readonly model?: readonly string[];
    readonly reasoningEffort?: string;
    // ...
}
```

Then, when constructing the child request, the local harness could merge the agent-specific effort into the resolved model configuration:

```ts
const modelConfiguration = modeModelId
    ? this.languageModelsService.getModelConfiguration(modeModelId)
    : undefined;

// Conceptually:
if (subagent?.reasoningEffort) {
    modelConfiguration.reasoningEffort = subagent.reasoningEffort;
}
```

The exact implementation can of course follow the existing model-configuration helpers and validation paths.

The same resolution should also be applied when a custom agent is selected directly from the agent picker, not only when it is invoked as a subagent.

## Why this matters

Currently, `reasoning-effort` is a supported `.agent.md` property, but whether it actually affects execution depends on the selected harness.

That makes shared custom agents difficult to reason about and can silently change latency, token usage, and behavior.

It is especially useful for multi-agent workflows where different roles intentionally use different reasoning budgets, for example:

```text
Explorer       -> medium
Implementation -> high
Code Review    -> xhigh
Planner        -> xhigh
```

These defaults should remain part of the agent definition regardless of whether the custom agent runs through the local VS Code harness or the Copilot Agent Host.

## Relationship to other issues

This is separate from #327099, which requests a dynamic reasoning-effort parameter on individual `runSubagent` invocations.

This issue is only about honoring the existing declarative `reasoning-effort` property from the target custom `.agent.md` file in the local harness.

Related:

* #313546 — Support reasoning effort configuration in custom `.agent.md` files
* #329263 — Support reasoning effort in custom agent files
* #327099 — Allow specifying reasoning effort per subagent invocation

title: Terminal and agent command output is inaccessible after output and scrollback limits are reached
body:
## Problem

When an agent runs a build or test command that produces substantial output, the terminal view and conversation surface impose output and scrollback limits. Once those limits are reached, the beginning of the command output is no longer visible or retrievable through the terminal surface.

This is not merely inconvenient for long-running builds. The first lines commonly contain the command, working directory, configuration, compiler invocation, and the first diagnostic. Losing them makes it impossible to review the complete execution record and can make the agent effectively unusable for debugging.

## Expected behavior

The complete command output should remain available through at least one reliable, user-visible mechanism. Suitable solutions could include:

- an expandable output artifact with unrestricted access;
- a command-specific transcript that can be opened and searched;
- controls to retrieve the beginning, middle, or end of output by byte or line range;
- a way to export the complete output without relying on terminal scrollback.

The terminal display may remain bounded for performance, but the underlying command transcript should not be discarded or made inaccessible.

## Actual behavior

After output or scrollback limits are reached, the first part of the output cannot be viewed in the terminal. The assistant may be able to summarize or store output separately, but the user cannot reliably inspect the complete result in the interface.

## Impact

This prevents trustworthy review of builds, tests, flashing prerequisites, and diagnostic commands. It is especially serious when the first diagnostic appears before the retained portion of the output.

## Environment

- Visual Studio Code on Linux
- GitHub Copilot agent workflow
- Integrated terminal commands producing long output

Please route this issue to the component responsible for retaining and exposing agent command output if it is not owned by the integrated terminal itself.

title: agentHost: rotate stale OTel session anchors
body:
## Problem

Agent Host emits one zero-duration `vscode.agent_host.session` span per session and parents every provider span under it for the session's whole lifetime. Some OTLP consumers keep the mapping needed to resolve that parent only for a limited time. Once it expires, they accept later child spans with HTTP 200 and never show them. I reproduced this with LangSmith: spans present in the local SQLite store were missing from the project.

## Behavior change

- Before each provider turn, the host re-exports the session's current anchor. Re-sending the identical span restores the consumer's parent mapping after an idle period.
- After 12 hours, the host issues a fresh anchor with a new span id and timestamp under the same trace id, keeping the anchor inside ingestion windows without rewriting history.
- Copilot and Codex pick up the current anchor at each turn. Claude gets it through its subprocess environment, so a rotated anchor triggers the existing resume-based rebuild before the next turn.
- Anchors are keyed by the chat's own resource. Peer and side chats keep one anchor each; a chat's rotation check and its rebuild always agree on that key.

## Trade-offs

- A consumer whose mapping has already expired may show a rotated anchor as the start of a new trace. Later spans stay visible instead of being dropped.
- Anchor re-export is queued, never awaited. In DB mode with an OTLP/HTTP JSON endpoint it shares the serialized forwarder with provider spans and arrives first. In pass-through mode the runtime exports on its own connection and ordering is best-effort.

Separate from github/copilot-cli#4726.

## Validation

- `tsc6 --noEmit` and `gulp compile-client` clean
- `agentHostOTelService.integrationTest.ts` and `claudeAgent.test.ts`: 308 passing, covering replay, rotation, Claude rebind, and peer-chat keying
- The peer-chat test fails against the previous lookup and passes with the fix

title: Agent host: a local slash command's output is never shown, leaving an empty turn
body:
### Summary

A local slash command runs to completion and its output is never shown. The turn ends with an empty assistant bubble, and nothing indicates the command produced anything.

I hit this with `/code-review`, which ran for 11 minutes, produced 13.6 KB of findings, and rendered nothing at all. The findings were recovered afterwards from the SDK transcript on disk.

### Where the output goes

The CLI records the result as a `system` entry with `subtype: local_command`, wrapping the payload:

```
<local-command-stdout>I've completed the review. Here are the findings.
```json
[ { "file": "...", "line": 5271, "summary": "..." }, ... ]
```

It also injects the standard preamble as a `user` entry:

```
<local-command-caveat>Caveat: The messages below were generated by the user while running local
commands. DO NOT respond to these messages or otherwise consider them in your response...
```

So the model correctly produces no assistant text, and the turn is genuinely empty.

### Why nothing renders

Both paths discard it, for defensible reasons that do not hold for stdout:

- **Replay**: `CLI_ECHO_MARKER_PATTERN` in `claudeReplayMapper.ts` matches `command-name`, `command-message`, `command-args`, `local-command-stdout`, `local-command-stderr` and `local-command-caveat`, and drops them so the workbench "doesn't render them as user turns". Correct for the echo markers, but it takes the command's actual output with them.
- **Live**: the recognised `system` subtypes are `compact_boundary` and `notification`. `local_command` is not among them, so the message maps to no signal.

The existing doc comment and the shipped e2e capture both use `<local-command-stdout>Set model to claude-opus-4.7</local-command-stdout>` as the example, which is exactly the case where dropping is harmless. It is not harmless when the command is a review, a build, or anything whose output is the point.

### Impact

Every local slash command is affected. In the terminal CLI the same output prints normally, so the behaviour differs between the two front ends for the same command.

### Suggested fix

Surface `<local-command-stdout>` (and `<local-command-stderr>`) as a response part on the active turn rather than discarding it, while continuing to drop the echo markers and the caveat. The caveat is what keeps the model from responding to it, so rendering the stdout does not change model behaviour, only what the user sees.

*AI disclosure: this issue and the related investigation were written with the assistance of AI.*

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: latest (1.136.x)
- VS Code Version: 1.136.1
- OS Version: Windows 11 x64
- Feature: Chat ask mode (MCP tool usage)
- Selected model: tokenrhythm/deepseek-v4-flash-0731
- Logs: attached below in the description

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Configure an MCP server at profile level (e.g. `@mozilla/firefox-devtools-mcp` with `--connect-existing --marionette-port 2828`).
2. Open multiple VS Code windows; some windows still hold a stale cached config of a **deleted workspace-level MCP server** (same underlying server, cached as `mcp.config.ws0.firefox-nightly` in workspace `state.vscdb` → `mcpToolCache`).
3. From Copilot Chat, call an MCP tool (e.g. `list_pages`).
4. Observe: the same tool call **alternates** between:
   - Reaching the server (server log shows `Executing tool: list_pages` → server-side error "No Marionette listener..."), and
   - Being rejected with **"disabled by the user"** (call never reaches the server).

Expected: tool availability should be consistent with the persisted authorization state.

Evidence:
- `mcpToolCache` in profile `state.vscdb` shows all 48 tools with `visibility: 3` (enabled), no disabled flags.
- Server log confirms the tool DID execute at 01:38:21: `[firefox-devtools-mcp] Executing tool: list_pages` → `Connecting to existing Firefox via Marionette...`.
- Minutes later, the exact same tool call is rejected as "disabled by the user" without any user action.
- `chat.mcp.autostart` is `never` in profile settings.
- The workspace-level cache still lists a deleted server (`mcp.config.ws0.firefox-nightly`), suggesting stale multi-window MCP state.

This looks like a sync issue between the MCP tool authorization cache, the per-window server connection state, and the Copilot-side permission check — likely triggered by multiple VS Code windows and a stale cached workspace-level MCP config.

title: [RFC] Update jschardet to v4
body:
I'm the author of jschardet and this is a completely new version that follows chardet's 7.x rewrite from scratch. Its main benefits are much improved accuracy across a wider range of supported encodings, alongside substantial memory and performance improvements. It's now written in TypeScript and ships with ESM support. This release also closes all but one of jschardet's open issues, most of which originated from vscode reports.

The main goal of this PR is to gauge interest in the upgrade and see whether this is a direction you'd like to take. I haven't released a stable v4.0.0 yet but I've been publishing release candidates in the form of v4.0.0-rc.X.

Main improvements over 3.1.4:

    Metric                     jschardet 3.1.4   jschardet 4.0.0(-rc.3)
    Accuracy (3,138 files)     43.1%             99.4%
    Speed                      126 files/s       780 files/s
    Language detection         —                 93.4%
    Peak memory                831.8 MiB         85.5 MiB
    Supported encodings        ~30               86
    MIME type detection        no                yes
    License                    LGPL-2.1+         0BSD

The trade-offs: the minified bundle grows from ~334 to ~1,141 KiB
(691 KiB gzipped) and cold start from ~30 to ~109 ms.

Detection changes (encoding.ts):
- jschardet >= 4 accepts a Uint8Array directly, in Node and the browser
  alike, so the manual latin1 round-trip (encodeLatin1) is no longer
  needed and is removed.
- Map jschardet's cp932/cp949 outputs onto iconv-lite's shiftjis/euckr.
- Widen the local `guessed` type to `{ encoding: string | null }` to match
  v4's detect() return type (its `encoding` is `string | null`).

Test fixtures:
- Change some.shiftjis.1.txt's trailing text (こんにちは -> 日本語)
  because v4 now detects the old sample as Shift-JIS even without
  candidate encodings, making the test vacuous; the new sample is
  Windows-1252 on its own and Shift-JIS with candidates, restoring the
  contrast.
- Correct some.shiftjis.1.txt's in-memory copy in files.ts: the
  Shift-JIS lead byte 0x82 had been written as the decimal literal 82
  (0x52), so the bytes never matched the on-disk file. v4 declines to
  guess the garbage, which v3 happened to tolerate.

title: Workspace picker redesign: prepare for multi-folder, local GitHub checkout, and PR review sessions

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Summary

The workspace picker redesign should make the common path—starting useful local work—clear and immediate, while leaving room for richer workspace and environment choices as those capabilities mature.

## Latest design decision

When `chat.agentSessions.consolidatedRemoteWorkspaces` is enabled, use one unified, searchable workspace picker instead of separate **Local** and **Remote** tabs. The unified list must retain one **Remote** entry with a flyout containing connected remote hosts plus **SSH...**, **Tunnels...**, **WSL...**, and other supported remote connection and management actions. Use **Start from Scratch** rather than **No workspace** for beginning without a backing workspace. In unified mode, collapse a generated `<repo>.worktrees/<branch>` recent onto an existing parent-repository entry, and place machine-specific remote workspace recents inside the **Remote** flyout so users with several development machines do not get a flat list of duplicate repository rows. Local folders, GitHub repository acquisition, Cloud repositories, and enabled remote targets should appear as actions in the same list. Category-specific entry points such as attaching a folder or GitHub context remain scoped. When the setting is disabled, preserve the existing tabbed picker.

## Priorities

| Priority | Area | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **P0 — Required** | Local checkout for GitHub repositories and independent environment selection | Selecting a repository that is not local currently does not lead to the expected usable desktop workflow. This is the primary gap. |
| **P1 — High value** | Local PR review sessions | This builds directly on local checkout and enables a concrete end-to-end workflow: inspect, run, review, edit, and push. |
| **P2 — Preserve existing behavior** | Keep multiple folder attachments clear and discoverable | The picker already supports attaching additional folders as agent context. This is a UX guardrail, not a new capability or a multi-root commitment. |
| **P3 — Nice to have** | Multi-select issues and start agent work | Useful power-user workflow with precedent in the GitHub Copilot app, but not necessary for the initial workspace picker redesign. |

## P0 — Local checkout for GitHub repositories

### Problem

When a user chooses a GitHub repository they have not checked out locally, they cannot currently proceed with the expected local workflow. Instead, Cloud is selected by default. For a desktop VS Code user, the more natural default is to clone/check out the repository and work on it locally.

Cloud is important and is likely to become more prominent as the environment experience matures, but it should be presented as an environment choice rather than being coupled to repository discovery or treated as the only path for a remote repository.

### Proposed direction

- Separate the flow into independent concepts:
  - **Source**: local folder, GitHub repository, pull request, or issue.
  - **Environment**: Local or Cloud.
  - **Harness/session type**: the agent or workflow that operates in that environment.
- For a GitHub repository that is not local:
  - Default the environment to **Local**.
  - Offer to clone/check out the repository, including a clear destination choice or an appropriate remembered/default clone location.
  - Keep **Cloud** visible as an explicit alternative.
- Do not encode Cloud as a special session type tied to GitHub repositories. The longer-term model should allow supported harnesses to run in the Cloud environment as capabilities become available.
- Remember an explicit user environment choice when appropriate, but avoid silently changing the default merely because the selected repository is remote.
- Clearly communicate clone, authentication, repository access, and environment availability errors rather than falling back to a different environment.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Choosing a GitHub repository that is not local offers a clone/checkout flow and defaults to Local.
- [ ] Cloud remains a visible, explicit environment choice rather than an implicit consequence of choosing a remote repository.
- [ ] Environment selection is modeled independently from source and harness/session type.
- [ ] Authentication, clone, checkout, and unsupported-environment failures are surfaced with actionable recovery.

## P1 — Local PR review sessions

### Problem

The new session page should allow a user to select a pull request and start a review-oriented session against a local checkout of its branch. The user should be able to inspect the diff, run the code and tests, review it, make changes, and push updates where permissions allow.

### Proposed direction

- Add pull requests as a source discoverable from the GitHub experience in the picker.
- Provide a **Review Pull Request** session intent/action.
- On Local:
  - Clone the repository if needed.
  - Fetch and check out the PR branch safely, accounting for forks and branches that cannot be pushed to directly.
  - Preserve PR metadata in the session so review context and relevant actions are available after launch and restoration.
- Allow the normal local toolchain: Files, Changes, terminal, run/debug, tests, review comments, edits, commits, and push when authorized.
- Offer Cloud as an explicit environment option when the selected harness and PR workflow are supported there.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can select a pull request and start a local PR review session against an appropriate checkout.
- [ ] The PR session retains enough metadata to support review, restoration, and relevant GitHub actions.
- [ ] Fork, permission, and read-only checkout states are clearly communicated.

## P2 — Preserve and clarify existing multiple-folder attachments

### Current behavior

The workspace picker already distinguishes between:

- **Select...** — chooses the single execution workspace/root for the session.
- **Attach Folder...** — adds another folder as agent context without changing the execution workspace.

Users can attach multiple additional folders, and those context attachments remain attached if the execution workspace changes. This already addresses the immediate need to let an agent work with context from more than one folder. It is intentionally different from a true multi-root workspace: Files, Changes/source control, and other surfaces continue to operate against the selected execution workspace.

### Direction for this redesign

- Preserve the existing ability to attach multiple folders.
- Keep the distinction between the execution workspace and attached folder context explicit in labels, pills/badges, and accessible descriptions.
- Make the existing attachment action discoverable from the redesigned picker; do not introduce another add-folder mechanism for the same purpose.
- Do not treat true multi-root support as a requirement for this redesign. If multi-root across Files, Changes, persistence, and session launch is pursued later, track it as separate end-to-end work.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can attach multiple folders as agent context while retaining one execution workspace.
- [ ] All attached folders remain visible and removable from the new-session experience.
- [ ] Changing the execution workspace does not silently discard additional folder attachments.
- [ ] The UI does not imply that attached folders become roots in Files or Changes.
- [ ] No duplicate **Add Folder** or **Attach Folder** affordance is introduced.

## P3 — Nice to have: multi-select issues and start agent work

### GitHub Copilot app precedent

The GitHub Copilot app's **My Work** view already provides a useful interaction model:

- Users select multiple issues and/or pull requests in the table.
- A selection toolbar opens an action palette/dropdown.
- The palette offers **Chat**, **New individual sessions**, and **New session**.
- For issues, it also supports choosing a target repository.
- **New individual sessions** creates one independently trackable workspace/session per selected item.
- **New session** creates one combined session. For multiple items in a configured local project, it uses a neutral worktree from the repository's default branch and attaches every selected item as context rather than treating the first issue as the primary task.

This is a better reference than exposing only one ambiguous “start working” action: users can choose whether the selected issues belong together or should run independently.

### Proposed direction

- Treat this as a follow-up enhancement, not a requirement for the initial workspace picker redesign.
- Add an issues source with multi-selection support when issue-driven workflows are prioritized.
- Once one or more issues are selected, expose an action palette/dropdown with:
  - **New Individual Sessions** — one independently trackable agent session per issue.
  - **New Session** — one session with all selected issues attached as context, for related work.
  - Optionally **Chat** — discuss the selected issues without creating a working checkout.
- If issues span repositories, require a clear target repository for a combined session; individual sessions can resolve their source and checkout per issue.
- Preserve issue URL, number, title, repository, and relevant body/context in the resulting session or sessions.
- For larger individual-session batches, show the scope before launch and report progress/failure per issue.

### Follow-up acceptance criteria

- [ ] The issues source supports selecting more than one issue.
- [ ] The selection action palette clearly distinguishes combined and individual session creation.
- [ ] Individual mode starts one independently trackable session per selected issue.
- [ ] Combined mode attaches every selected issue as context and uses an explicit target repository.
- [ ] Batch launch reports success or failure per issue and permits retrying failed items without relaunching successful ones.

## UX principles

- Optimize the default for the most common desktop expectation: selecting remote code should result in a usable local checkout.
- Keep source, environment, and harness choices conceptually independent.
- Reveal complexity progressively; do not make users configure every dimension when sensible defaults exist.
- Do not expose selections that lead to partially supported or misleading session states.
- Future-proof the design without making future capabilities prerequisites for solving today's core workflow.

## Follow-up work to identify

### P0/P1

- Local clone destination and repository reuse behavior.
- GitHub authentication and repository/PR discovery.
- PR checkout behavior for same-repository branches versus forks.
- Push permissions and safe behavior for read-only PRs.
- Capability negotiation between environments and harnesses.
- Session restoration when the checkout moves, disappears, or changes branches.

### P2

- Validate the existing multiple-folder attachment flow in the redesigned picker.
- Ensure execution-workspace and attached-context terminology remains unambiguous.
- Track any future true multi-root work separately across Files, Changes/source control, persistence, and session launch.

### P3

- GitHub issue discovery and filtering.
- Combined versus individual session defaults.
- Limits or confirmation thresholds for large issue batches.
- Mapping issues from multiple repositories to checkouts, worktrees, environments, and concurrent sessions.

title: Spare a background subagent's in-flight tool call from the turn-end wipe
body:
`clearPending` drops all cross-message tool attribution on every `result` envelope. A background subagent outlives the turn that spawned it, so its inner tool call is still in flight and its result is still coming, but its entry is wiped along with the genuinely orphaned ones.

## Why it matters

The registry exists because a `tool_use` and its `tool_result` arrive in different SDK messages, so the tool name, parsed input and invocation message have to survive between them. Once the entry is gone, the late result renders with the generic past-tense message instead of the real one, and live output diverges from what replay produces from the same transcript.

## The precedent

`drainForegroundSpawns` is called from `mapResult` two lines after `clearPendingToolCalls`, and already makes exactly this distinction:

> Turn-end cleanup: remove and return foreground spawns whose completion never closed them. Background spawns survive across turns by design (their completion arrives later via `system.task_notification`).

The subagent registry keeps that state; the tool call registry simply never consulted it.

## The change

`clearPending` takes an optional lookup and skips entries whose parent spawn is background, leaving every other orphan drained and warned exactly as before. The lookup is declared as a narrow local interface rather than importing the subagent registry, to avoid a cycle between the two modules. `clearPendingToolCalls` already runs before `drainForegroundSpawns`, so the spawn and its inner edges are still present when the check happens.

## Tests

- `clearPending spares an inner tool of a background subagent and still drains the rest` fails without the change.
- `clearPending still drains an inner tool whose parent subagent is foreground` is the control and passes either way.

The suite goes from 12 passing with 1 failing to 13 passing, and both pre-existing `clearPending` tests are unaffected. No new type errors.

title: Do not mark a denied subagent tool call as a subagent
body:
A denied `Agent` or `Task` call still gets a subagent marker attached to its result, so on restore the host registers a subagent chat whose transcript can never exist.

## What happens

`toolKind` is derived from the tool **name**, with no regard for the outcome, and `_attachToolResult` pushes `ToolResultContentType.Subagent` unconditionally. On restore, `_registerRestoredSubagentSummaries` scans replayed turns for that marker and registers a chat with a lazy resolver, and the resolver throws `Subagent transcript is not available yet` forever, because nothing was ever spawned.

Since #334312 that is no longer fatal to the session, but the phantom chat is still registered, still fails to `subscribe`, and still shows in the session's chat list as a subagent that never produces anything.

## How it was hit

Auto mode could not classify an `Agent` call and denied it:

```
"...temporarily unavailable, so auto mode cannot determine the safety of Agent right now..."
"toolDenialKind": "automode-unavailable"
```

The SDK transcript for that session is 47 lines with zero `isSidechain` entries, confirming no subagent ran. Any denial reaches this the same way, so a permission rule or a user rejecting the call does too.

## The change

`is_error` alone is not the right test: it also covers a subagent that **started and then failed**, and those children have real transcripts that must still be linked on restore.

The SDK stamps `agentId: <hex>` on the tool_result of a call that actually spawned, which is what `scanTranscriptForAgentIds` already keys on through the exported `SUBAGENT_ID_SUFFIX_REGEX`. A pre-spawn denial is therefore the case with an error and no agentId:

```ts
const spawned = !isError || SUBAGENT_ID_SUFFIX_REGEX.test(resultText);
if (isSubagent && spawned) {
```

`resultText` is already computed immediately above for the past-tense message, so nothing new is derived.

## Tests

- `Fixture 5c: a denied Agent tool_use produces no subagent marker` asserts the call is still recognised as a subagent by name, that `success` is `false`, and that no marker is attached.
- `Fixture 5d: an Agent that spawned and then failed keeps its subagent marker` is the failed-after-spawn case, and fails against an `is_error`-only condition.

Fixtures 5 and 5b continue to pass, so successful spawns are unchanged. The suite is 30 passing. No new type errors.

title: Fix terminal prompt duplication when resizing the terminal panel
body:
Fixes #329946 (partial — see "Known limitations" below)

## Summary

When the terminal panel is resized, the shell prompt can be duplicated / new prompt lines created on every resize instead of the buffer reflowing cleanly. Two causes in the terminal resize path:

1. **Redundant PTY resizes on every layout event.** `TerminalResizeDebouncer.resize()` fired a resize even when the grid dimensions did not change (e.g. while dragging the panel), sending a PTY resize (SIGWINCH) on every layout event. Shells repaint the prompt on SIGWINCH, so this produced a storm of prompt redraws while dragging.

2. **Horizontal resizes debounced too briefly.** The debounced horizontal resize fired after 100ms, but shells such as zsh need longer than that to fully process a prompt redraw after a resize. When resizes arrived back-to-back, the shell computed its prompt redraw from a stale terminal width, which misplaces the erase/rewrite and leaves duplicated prompt fragments in the buffer.

## Changes

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalResizeDebouncer.ts`:
- Skip the resize entirely (and cancel any pending debounced resize) when the requested `cols`/`rows` equal the current grid — no more redundant PTY resizes / SIGWINCH storms while dragging.
- Only fire the immediate Y-resize when `rows` actually changed, and only schedule the debounced X-resize when `cols` actually changed.
- Increase `DebounceResizeXDelay` from 100ms to 300ms so the shell's prompt redraw is fully processed between consecutive resizes.

## Verification

- Reproduced the duplication headlessly with a real zsh 5.9 and bash shell in a pty driving the bundled xterm.js: with the 100ms debounce the buffer ended with 3 prompt copies after a shrink/grow/shrink cycle; with 300ms exactly 1 copy.
- Verified in a running Code OSS instance (launched with playwright over CDP): resizing the bottom-panel terminal (long prompt, shrink/grow cycles, continuous drags) reflows cleanly with no duplication.

## Known limitations (honest assessment)

This fixes the common cases (panel resizing at moderate widths, continuous drags). It does **not** fix every duplication scenario:

- **Extreme-narrow terminals with colored prompts** (e.g. terminal docked in the side panel and shrunk to its minimum width, ~15-20 columns, with a colored `PS1`/`PROMPT`): the prompt can still duplicate. Root cause: xterm.js deliberately does not reflow the cursor line on non-Windows (`reflowCursorLine=false`), so the prompt is a single buffer row rendered wrapped across several visual rows. The shell's redraw (readline/zsh) operates on visual rows, so its erase/rewrite misses rows and fragments accumulate. Enabling `reflowCursorLine` makes this worse due to https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5295 (cursor mispositioned on reflow of cursor line), which the xterm.js maintainers have declined to fix. Upstream VS Code has no fix for this either; it would require a change in xterm.js or readline.

title: dictation: fix indefinite hangs by adding timeouts to Foundry Local native calls
body:
## What

On-device (`nemo`/Foundry Local) dictation could hang indefinitely with no error surfaced to the user — the toolbar spinner would just spin forever, or clicking Stop/Cancel would do nothing.

## Why

`LocalTranscriptionService` (the utility-process side of dictation) awaits several native `foundry-local-sdk` calls that have no `AbortSignal` and no timeout of their own:

- the model catalog lookup (`manager.catalog.getModel`)
- `model.load()` (explicitly called out in an existing code comment as having "no AbortSignal")
- `session.start()`
- each `session.append()` call — these are chained serially through `_appendChain` to preserve audio order, so one wedged append blocks every later chunk **and** `stop()`, which awaits the whole chain
- the result stream's `next()` (via `for await...of session.getStream()`) — `stop()` awaits the consumer promise, so a stream that silently stops yielding (without throwing) hangs Stop forever
- `session.stop()` / `session.dispose()`

If any of these stalls — a proxy/firewall silently dropping packets, a wedged native addon, a driver hiccup during model load, etc. — the corresponding promise never settles. Since `start()`/`pushAudio()`/`stop()`/`cancel()` all await these calls directly or transitively, the whole feature hangs with no recovery short of restarting VS Code.

The one existing exception was the native runtime tarball download, which already has a `DOWNLOAD_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` guard (see `foundryLocalRuntime.ts`) — this PR extends the same pattern to the remaining unguarded native calls.

## Change

Adds a small `withTimeout()` helper and races each of the calls above against a bounded timeout (30s for catalog lookup, 120s for model load, 15s for session start/append/teardown, 60s inactivity for the result stream). A timeout now rejects with a descriptive error that flows through the existing error-handling path (`classifyModelError`, which gains a new `'timeout'` code) exactly like any other model/session failure, so the existing UI (progress ring, error notification, `_failModelSession`) picks it up instead of hanging silently.

This does not cancel the underlying native call (the SDK gives us no way to) — it only unblocks whichever caller is waiting on it so the failure is surfaced and the session can be reset/retried.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes (the one remaining reported error, in `mcpSamplingLog.test.ts`, is pre-existing and unrelated to this change).
- This service wraps a native addon with no existing unit test harness (only `foundryLocalRuntime` and `foundryLocalModelImport` have tests), so validation here is via typecheck + code review; the change is a set of surgical `Promise.race` wraps around existing await points and does not alter behavior on the non-timeout success path.

## Summary

- limit Copilot debug exports to the current process log and one previous matching log
- prompt for the export destination immediately while log collection runs concurrently
- keep collection progress visible and separate destination selection from writing for desktop and browser exports

Trace-level Copilot process logs can grow to hundreds of megabytes per process. title: Clear stale focus and selection in the chat changed-files list
Fix tab close button stuck showing "Close Others" after focus changes

labels.name: release-cherry-pick
labels.description: Automated cherry-pick between release and main branches

body:
## Description

Alt+hover swaps a tab's **Close** action for **Close Others**. Both inputs to that swap could go stale across a focus change: `redrawTabAction()` read `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey` at paint time (the Alt `keyup` is delivered to whichever app you Alt+Tab'd into), and `hoveredTabIndex` was only cleared by a real `mouseleave`. Coming back to the window without moving the mouse could therefore leave the `x` armed as "Close Others", so a plain click silently closed every other editor in the group.

### Changes — `MultiEditorTabsControl`

- **Local Alt state.** A `isAltPressed` field, fed by the `ModifierKeyEmitter` event, replaces the two on-demand reads of `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey`. It is the single source of truth for the swap and redraws the hovered tab when it flips.
- **Give up the swap on focus loss.** `IHostService.onDidChangeFocus(false)` clears both the Alt state and the hovered tab, so a hover left over from before the focus change cannot be re-armed by Alt state re-established on return. Re-hovering a tab arms it again as usual.
- **Re-validate Alt from mouse events.** `mousemove`/`mousedown` on the tabs container carry the real modifier state even when a `keyup` was missed entirely — this covers macOS Mission Control, where the window may never see a `blur`.

The mouse listeners are registered in the **capture** phase because `BaseActionViewItem` calls `EventHelper.stop(e, true)` on `mousedown`; a bubble-phase listener never sees a press on the close button itself, which is precisely the reported "click without moving the mouse" case.

```ts
for (const eventType of [EventType.MOUSE_MOVE, EventType.MOUSE_DOWN]) {
	this._register(addDisposableListener(tabsContainer, eventType, (e: MouseEvent) => {
		this.setAltPressed(e.altKey);
	}, true));
}
```

In the stale-Alt case the capture handler swaps the action item mid-`mousedown`, so that first click is swallowed rather than executing "Close Others" — the icon is then correct and the next click closes the single tab.

`EditorTabsControl.hostService` becomes `protected` so the subclass can use it.

### Tests

`src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` covers the baseline swap plus the focus-loss, mouse-move and action-mousedown paths; each regression test was checked to fail with its corresponding part of the change reverted.

### Notes for reviewers

- After returning from another application the swap requires a fresh hover (move to another tab, or leave and re-enter). This is the behaviour suggested in the issue and is what makes a stale hover unexploitable.
- `menuEntryActionViewItem.ts` has the same latent staleness pattern; left untouched to keep this scoped to tabs.

Set `editor.wordWrapIndicator` to `true` to turn it on; it only has an effect while `editor.wordWrap` is enabled. ## How it works ### Rendering Rendering is done by `WordWrapIndicatorOverlay`, a `DynamicViewOverlay` registered on the content overlay layer in `view.ts` alongside the selection and whitespace overlays. `prepareRender` walks the view lines of the viewport and produces one HTML string per line. A line gets a glyph only when `continuesWithWrappedLine` is set — that is, when it is followed by a soft wrap rather than by a real line break, and is not the last line of the model. The glyph itself is a single `
` holding U+21A9 LEFTWARDS ARROW WITH HOOK. Its content-relative `left` is the effective wrapping column multiplied by the font's typical half-width character width, so every glyph stays aligned with the boundary that produced the wrap. Horizontal scrolling moves the glyph with the document content instead of pinning it to the viewport edge. Its height comes from `getLineHeightForLineNumber`, so lines carrying a custom line height keep the indicator vertically aligned. ### Color `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` is a new theme colour that defaults to `editorWhitespace.foreground`, so out of the box the indicator is as muted as rendered whitespace, while themes can still override it on its own. ## Known Limitations The indicator marks the wrapping boundary rather than the exact end of the rendered text, so a segment that wraps at whitespace can leave a gap before the glyph. When a fixed `wordWrapColumn` lies beyond the viewport, the indicator remains offscreen until horizontal scrolling reveals that column. The indicator is a visual-only overlay; it has no equivalent representation for screen readers or the minimap. ## Other Editors - Visual Studio - Notepad++ - IntelliJ IDEA Word wrap indicator is shown at the beginning of the wrapped line Does not have word wrap indicator: - XCode - Sublime Text --- ## Manual checklist before marking ready for review - [x] Toggle `editor.wordWrapIndicator` live with a wrapped file open: the glyph appears and disappears without needing a reload. - [x] Glyph stays aligned with the effective wrapping column at several `editor.fontSize` values and with a proportional font (`editor.fontFamily` set to a non-monospace family). - [x] Correct with variable line heights. - [x] Interacts sanely with `editor.renderWhitespace: 'all'` — the glyph should not collide with a trailing whitespace dot. - [x] Not selectable and not copied when selecting across a wrapped line (`pointer-events: none` covers hit testing; verify the clipboard). - [x] Inline suggestions / inlay hints / injected text on a wrapped line do not push the glyph to the wrong position. - [x] `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` shows up in `workbench.colorCustomizations` IntelliSense and overriding it takes effect. - [x] Legible in Dark+, Light+, and both high contrast themes — the inherited `editorWhitespace.foreground` is deliberately faint, so confirm it is visible enough in HC without being noisy in the default themes. - [x] Accessibility: confirm the glyph is not announced by the screen reader as line content. ## Feedback from standup Team members mentioned in the standup that they would prefer having the word wrap indicator on the left-hand side in the gutter instead of at the wrapping column on the right. The issue with this idea is that it requires the gutter to be present, so people with no gutter would not see this, and sometimes people only show every 5 lines so the word wrap indicator would look weird.
